reason: Both films use the same narration, authored assets and event clock. Option b carries the order through physically coherent space and keeps people and results readable. At 0.2 to 1.8 s its overhead floor plan shows footprints leaving the host stand and the door swinging shut, so the walk-out is pictured, not implied. At 5.0 to 7.6 s a close shot puts a blank order pad in front of two readable waiting diners. At 19.2 to 21.2 s an over-the-shoulder seated guest with an attached arm taps Chow mein, and at 22.0 to 23.4 s a large Paid card lands on a legible phone. At 24.6 to 25.6 s the floor plan shows the paid phone on the guest's table and a dashed path to the printer on the counter, which makes pay first, cook second spatially literal. At 36.6 to 37.6 s the tip jar fills next to the printer, which still holds the Chow mein ticket. The closing detail at 58.4 to 60.4 s joins that ticket to the jar with its owner says and no record shown tags.
rejected_reason: Option a performs the same events, but it breaks spatial continuity and hides results. At 24.6 to 25.6 s and again at 35.0 to 36.4 s a hand-held phone on a long rigid arm floats inside the kitchen beside the printer and the jar. At 44.4 to 45.8 s the pen-hand forearm covers the rule card text, then parks across the completed circle. Between 51.0 and 51.2 s the hesitating hand vanishes and the phone jumps from the hand to lying flat on the table. The hook (0.0 to 7.6 s) never shows anyone leave: the door shuts on an empty room and the diners are about 40 px tall.
